quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Traffic signal ahead.
Stop completely and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protects your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes in a crash. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Go straight across the tracks in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight across the tracks in your lane.
questions.explanation: It is safest to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks going straight in your lane. Changing angle may push you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn at night.
Help other drivers see you better.
Do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you are farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it tells the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not matter because it does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it tells the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This may tell the other driver to come back into your lane too early.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
Divided roadway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Position themselves where other drivers can see them.
Speed up to get through the intersection quickly.
Get ready on the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to get through the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, position yourself where you are most visible. Get ready on the clutch and brakes to react quickly. Slow down. Do not change speed or position suddenly because other drivers may misunderstand your actions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road.
A paved driveway.
Dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road.
questions.explanation: Poor traction occurs on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal covers or plates.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcyclist has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid parked cars and people on the right.
Motorcycles can stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcyclist can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid parked cars and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars on your right, you can ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only ride on the left side if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: Good eye or face shield protection must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and limit your view.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to know what is around you. Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle like a motorcycle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can judge your speed and location correctly.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Turning too fast may cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's transmission must be in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's safety before every ride. Test each brake control to make sure it activates the brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group, inexperienced riders should:

options.text: Lead the group.
Be near the front of the group.
Be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then re-apply pressure to the brake slowly and steadily.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger do?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Look ahead at your path.
Be ready to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals and brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which lane position best keeps other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your space. When following a car, the center position puts you in the middle of the driver's rearview mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the part of the lane that puts you in another driver's view as early as possible.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of the lane behind a car, drivers can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other drivers you are riding near them.
To help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping where they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping where they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash it before slowing for a sharp turn off a highway or any time you slow down unexpectedly.

questions.question: What is the illegal blood alcohol content (BAC) level for operating a motorcycle?

options.text: 0.08 percent.
0.1 percent.
0.3 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: In California, it is illegal for anyone age 21 or older to operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. For anyone under 21, the limit is 0.01 percent. Riding may be unsafe even below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does the Motorcycle Safety Foundation's "SEE" strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy helps riders make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.
